text:
maria: Heads-up: Large EU customer needs a tenant-pinned model + signed artifact bundle by EOW. Compliance requires reproducible outputs for a small set of canonical prompts.
kim: Timeline short. Recommend pinning an existing stable build (v2.1) and producing a "forensics-lite" bundle rather than retraining.
leo: Agreed. I can spin up a 4-GPU canary pool for 12h tomorrow to run deterministic checks.
rachel: Ops: we can expose a tenant-scoped route and return an X-Model-Hash header. Also can include kernel hashes if eng-runtime can expose them.
maria: Customer wants exact-match on 20 canonical prompts, plus latency p95 < 250ms on their EU traffic. They also want model hash, quantization recipe, and server config in the bundle.
kim: Proposed bench: 20 canonical prompts + 100 sampled prompts. Run each variant twice: unquantized GPU, quantized GPU, and quantized CPU. Assert token-trace equality for canonical set after normalization and capture divergence metrics for sampled set.
leo: I'll capture kernel versions and perf traces. If quantized builds show non-determinism, we either pin kernels or offer unquantized dedicated pool as a commercial option.
rachel: I'll prepare tenant route manifest and artifact signing flow (KMS). deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: model=redwood/v2.1-2025-03-01 pool=canary-4g window=12h.
maria: Next steps: (1) kim+leo run forensics-lite (tomorrow), (2) rachel enable tenant route + signing (tomorrow), (3) maria draft comms and negotiation options for customer (today). I'll update customer with plan and ETA.
kim: Add a human-readable README to the bundle explaining tests, commands, and expected hashes.
rachel: Looping legal if bundle needs signature wording.
maria: Thanks team. Post blockers here and escalate if needed. :thumbsup:
